subtype: Stage 4: Fear of loss of freedom [Actor]
passage:
When Mehak first said, "What if we just got one flat instead of two?", I said, "Yes, obviously," and meant it. Then over the next month I got quieter and quieter.
I love her. I love waking up to her humming and the way she argues with the TV news. But every time she sent me a listing, something in my chest tightened, like a door slowly swinging shut. No more evenings alone with my music loud. No more coming home to just me.
I didn't say anything, which I now know was the problem. Mehak thought I was losing interest. One night she asked, "Do you not want this?" and I finally said it: "I do. And I'm scared. Both."
She laughed, a bit shakily. "Thank god. I thought it was only the second one." After that, Disha's fear became something we could plan around, instead of something Mehak had to guess.

qa.a: Mehak suggested getting one flat instead of two.

qa.q: Why did Disha go quiet over that month?
qa.a: Disha loved Mehak but felt a door closing on time alone and freedom, and didn't know how to say both feelings at once.

qa.q: What changed once Disha said 'I do. And I'm scared. Both.'?
qa.a: The mixed feelings became something they could plan around together, instead of Mehak guessing that Disha was losing interest.

qa.q: What was Mehak feeling while Disha stayed quiet?
qa.a: Mehak thought Disha was losing interest and was worried, which is why her laugh was shaky with relief once Disha explained.

grounding: Shows one partner growing quiet as moving in together nears, feeling love and a closing door, and saying it before the silence does harm.

subtype: Stage 4: Fear of loss of freedom [Actor]
passage:
Counselling note. Karthik, 25. Session 1, self-referred.
Karthik says he and Sabina have been together two years and plan to move in together in April. He describes her warmly and smiles when he talks about her. But he has noticed he's become quieter in recent weeks, avoids the flat-hunting spreadsheet and has cancelled two viewings with work excuses.
He said: "I love her. But when I picture our names on the lease, it's like a door closing. I haven't told her. I don't want her to think I don't love her."
We discussed that mixed feelings before a big step are common, and that the bigger risk is Sabina reading his silence as a lack of love. He agreed to tell her this week, in his own words, before the next viewing.
Plan: review how the conversation went next session.

qa.q: How many viewings has Karthik cancelled?
qa.a: Karthik has cancelled two viewings with work excuses.

qa.q: What is Karthik afraid Sabina will think?
qa.a: Karthik is afraid Sabina will think he doesn't love her if he admits his fear of a door closing.

qa.q: Why did the counsellor encourage Karthik to speak to Sabina soon?
qa.a: Hiding the mixed feelings is the bigger risk, since Sabina may read the silence and cancelled viewings as lost love; saying it early is kinder.

qa.q: How might Sabina be interpreting Karthik's cancelled viewings?
qa.a: Sabina may be confused or hurt, wondering if Karthik is losing interest, because she can't see the fear behind the work excuses.

grounding: Illustrates a young man becoming quieter as moving in nears, loving his partner yet fearing lost freedom, and being encouraged to say so early.
